headline: Endangered Houston Toad Spotted After 50 Years
meta_description: A Houston toad, one of America's most endangered amphibians, was spotted in restored habitat for the first time in over 50 years.
summary_short: After conservationists released 170,000 eggs in April, the critically endangered Houston toad has returned to its habitat—a milestone in species recovery.
body:
A Houston toad, one of America's most endangered amphibians, has been spotted in restored habitat for the first time in over 50 years—a major milestone for the struggling species.

The sighting followed a deliberate conservation effort in April, when researchers released 170,000 eggs into the revitalized area. This coordinated breeding and release program represents years of careful work to bring the species back from the brink of extinction. The presence of Houston toads in the restored habitat suggests that conditions there are finally suitable for the amphibians to thrive again.

The rediscovery offers hope that intensive conservation strategies can reverse the decline of even the most critically endangered species, provided their habitats are protected and restored.
